theory.intro: Some ratio problems give the **difference** between two shares instead of the total. Because every part is worth the same, the difference is worth $m-n$ parts — so divide the difference by $m-n$ to find $1$ part, then multiply to reach whatever the question asks for.
facts: In the ratio $m:n$ with $m>n$, the gap between the two shares is $m-n$ parts.
If two shares are in the ratio $5:3$ and one is $10$ more than the other, then $2\text{ parts}=10$, so $1\text{ part}=5$.
'$30$ fewer' and '$30$ more' describe the same gap — the smaller share is always the one with fewer parts.
Once $1$ part is known the shares are $m$ parts and $n$ parts, and the total is $m+n$ parts.
On a bar model the gap is the run of cells the longer bar has that the shorter bar does not.
steps: Subtract the ratio parts to find how many parts the given difference represents.
Divide the difference by that number of parts to find the value of $1$ part.
Multiply to find the share, the total or the difference that was asked for.

development.question_text: A length of rope is cut into two pieces in the ratio $7:4$. The longer piece is $4.5$ m longer than the shorter piece. How long was the rope before it was cut?
development.solution_text:
$7-4=3\text{ parts}$
$3\text{ parts}=4.5\text{ m}$
$1\text{ part}=1.5\text{ m}$
$11\text{ parts}=16.5\text{ m}$

development.question_text: Two collectors share some trading cards in the ratio $9:6$. One of them receives $21$ more cards than the other. How many cards does each collector receive?
development.solution_text:
$9:6$
$=3:2$
$3-2=1\text{ part}$
$1\text{ part}=21$
$3\text{ parts}=63\text{ cards}$
$2\text{ parts}=42\text{ cards}$

development.question_text: A drink is made from cordial and water in the ratio $1:9$. There is $720$ mL more water than cordial in the jug. How many full $250$ mL glasses can be poured from the jug?
development.solution_text:
$9-1=8\text{ parts}$
$8\text{ parts}=720\text{ mL}$
$1\text{ part}=90\text{ mL}$
$10\text{ parts}=900\text{ mL}$
$900\div250=3.6$
Only $3$ full glasses can be poured.

development.question_text: Two employees share a bonus in the ratio $5:8$. One of them receives $\$360$ more than the other. What was the total bonus?
A rectangular garden has its length and width in the ratio $5:2$. The length is $18$ m more than the width. Find the area of the garden.
development.solution_text:
$5-2=3\text{ parts}$
$3\text{ parts}=18\text{ m}$
$1\text{ part}=6\text{ m}$
$5\text{ parts}=30\text{ m}$
$2\text{ parts}=12\text{ m}$
$A=30\times12$
$=360\text{ m}^{2}$

mastery.question_text: Ben and Kira share some stickers in the ratio $5:2$. Ben then gives Kira $21$ stickers, and now they have exactly the same number each. How many stickers were shared altogether?
mastery.solution_text:
Ben loses $21$ and Kira gains $21$, so the original gap was $2\times21=42$.
$5-2=3\text{ parts}$
$3\text{ parts}=42$
$1\text{ part}=14$
$7\text{ parts}=98\text{ stickers}$

mastery.question_text: Three charities share a donation in the ratio $4:6:9$. The largest share is $\$75$ more than the smallest share. How much more does the middle charity receive than the smallest?

Hana and Yuki share a sum of money in the ratio $3:8$, and Yuki receives $\$120$ more than Hana. They then share the same total again, this time in the ratio $5:6$. How much more does Hana receive the second time?
mastery.solution_text:
$8-3=5\text{ parts}$
$5\text{ parts}=\$120$
$1\text{ part}=\$24$
$3\text{ parts}=\$72$ for Hana at first
$11\text{ parts}=\$264$ in total
$11\text{ new parts}=\$264$
$1\text{ new part}=\$24$
$5\text{ new parts}=\$120$ for Hana now
$120-72=\$48$ more
